title: Fixed-object sorted-algebra presentation of simplicial categories
statement: Fix a universe and a small set $O$. Use the notion of a sorted algebraic theory and its strict simplicial algebras from [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model]. For a finite list $\alpha=((x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_m,y_m))$ of elements of $O\times O$, let $P_\alpha$ be the ordinary category on $O$ freely generated by labelled arrows $e_j:x_j\to y_j$: morphisms are finite composable words in the $e_j$, including empty identity words, and composition is concatenation. Let $T_O$ be the opposite of the small category whose objects are these finite lists and whose morphisms from $\alpha$ to $\beta$ are functors $P_\alpha\to P_\beta$ fixing $O$. Concatenation of lists gives finite products in $T_O$, and the empty list gives its terminal object. Thus $T_O$ is an $O\times O$-sorted algebraic theory, with distinguished sort the one-term list $((x,y))$. There is an equivalence between the category of finite-product-preserving functors $T_O\to\mathrm{sSet}$ and the category $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ of small simplicial categories on $O$ and simplicial functors fixing $O$. Under this equivalence, evaluation at $((x,y))$ is naturally isomorphic to mapping-set evaluation $A\mapsto A(x,y)$. The operations of $T_O$ encode ordinary identities and composition; simplicial operators belong to the simplicial-set values of a model. No nonemptiness assumption on $O$, and no restriction $x\ne y$, is imposed.

source.place: Bergner, Rigidification of algebras over multi-sorted theories, Example 3.5 and Definition 3.6, printed pp.1937-1938; introduction, printed p.1926, states the simplicial interpretation. The finite-list free-category presentation spells out this example, using the opposite of the free-category subcategory. No Stacks tag states this identification. Read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let C_O be the category whose objects are finite lists of labelled pairs from O times O and whose arrows are functors between the corresponding free categories P_alpha that fix O. Because O and every list are small, the arrows are sets, and composition is ordinary functor composition. The free category on the disjoint union of two finite lists is the coproduct of the two free categories in C_O: a functor out of P_(alpha concatenated beta) is uniquely a pair of functors out of P_alpha and P_beta agreeing on the common object set. The empty list gives the discrete category on O, initial in C_O. Passing to T_O=C_O^op therefore makes list concatenation a finite product and the empty list terminal; the one-term list ((x,y)) is the distinguished sort. This also covers an empty O and lists containing loops x=y.

source.place: Bergner, Example 3.5 and Definition 3.6, printed pp.1937-1938; the finite-list free-category construction is the explicit opposite-category presentation of that example.

proof.text: By the definition of a strict simplicial algebra over a finite-product theory, a model A of T_O is a finite-product-preserving functor to simplicial sets. Its value on a list alpha is consequently canonically the product of its values on the one-term lists in alpha. In C_O, the functor P_(x,z) to P_((x,y),(y,z)) sending its generator to the word e_(y,z) after e_(x,y) induces in T_O a map from the product of the (x,y)- and (y,z)-sorts to the (x,z)-sort; the functors sending a loop generator to an identity induce the unit maps. The equalities of functors expressing associativity and the two unit laws become the corresponding equalities of simplicial maps. Thus the singleton-sort values of A carry exactly the identities and associative simplicial composition of a simplicial category on O.

source.place: Bergner, Example 3.5, Definition 3.6 and the evaluation/free-algebra discussion, printed pp.1937-1938,1942.

proof.text: Conversely, let B be a simplicial category on O. For a list alpha set A_B(alpha) to the product over its entries (x_j,y_j) of B(x_j,y_j), with the empty product the terminal simplicial set. For a morphism of T_O represented by a functor P_beta to P_alpha fixing O, send a tuple of alpha-arrows to the tuple of beta-arrows obtained by interpreting each generator of P_beta as its finite composable word in the alpha-generators and composing in B. Functoriality of these maps follows from substitution of words, and preservation of concatenation products is immediate. The identity and composition operations recovered in Step 2 are the original ones of B, while starting from A and applying this construction returns A because every morphism in a free category is a unique finite word. Hence the two constructions are inverse on objects.

source.place: Bergner, Example 3.5 and Definition 3.6, printed pp.1937-1938; explicit word-substitution verification for the finite-list presentation.

proof.text: A morphism of strict T_O-algebras is a natural transformation, hence is determined by its components on the singleton sorts and the naturality squares for the unit and composition maps. These are exactly an identity-on-O simplicial functor between the associated simplicial categories. Conversely every such simplicial functor gives a natural transformation by taking products on finite lists. Therefore the constructions define an equivalence of categories, and evaluation at the distinguished singleton sort is naturally the mapping simplicial set B(x,y). No step uses x different from y or a nonempty object set, so the stated edge cases remain included.

source.place: Bergner, Definition 3.6 and Example 3.5, printed pp.1937-1938; introduction, printed p.1926.

proof_origin.place: Bergner, Rigidification of algebras over multi-sorted theories, Example 3.5 and Definition 3.6, printed pp.1937-1938, with the finite-list free-category construction and word-substitution verification expanded here.

lean.statement: theorem cone_sorted_theory_identification (O : Type u) : (∀ α β : Lists O, Nonempty (IsLimit (concatFan α β))) ∧ (∀ α : Lists O, Nonempty (IsLimit (listFan α))) ∧ ∃ (p : HasFiniteProducts (Theory O)) (g : ∀ X : Theory O, ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → O × O), Nonempty (X ≅ ∏ᶜ fun i : Fin n => sort (f i))), ∃ E : StrictSimplicialAlgebra (sortedTheory p g) ≌ SSet.Bergner.Fixed O, ∃ e : ∀ x y : O, evaluation (T := sortedTheory p g) (x, y) ≅ E.functor ⋙ SSet.Bergner.mappingSetEvaluation x y, (∀ (A : StrictSimplicialAlgebra (sortedTheory p g)) (x : O) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (t : (A.1.obj (op [])).obj n), ((e x x).hom.app A).app n ((A.1.map (unitOperation x)).app n t) = ((E.functor.obj A).id x).app n PUnit.unit) ∧ (∀ (A : StrictSimplicialAlgebra (sortedTheory p g)) (x y z : O) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (t : (A.1.obj (op [(x, y), (y, z)])).obj n), ((e x z).hom.app A).app n ((A.1.map (compOperation x y z)).app n t) = ((E.functor.obj A).comp x y z).app n (((e x y).hom.app A).app n ((A.1.map (projection [(x, y), (y, z)] 0)).app n t), ((e y z).hom.app A).app n ((A.1.map (projection [(x, y), (y, z)] 1)).app n t)))
